questions.q: Why does the Moon appear to change its shape throughout the month?
questions.a: The Moon appears to change shape because it orbits the Earth, and our view of the side lit by the Sun changes as it moves. A student saying "the Moon grows or shrinks" reveals a failure to understand that the Moon is a solid sphere whose actual shape remains constant.

questions.q: If you see a "New Moon," where is the Moon located in relation to the Earth and the Sun?
questions.a: The Moon is located between the Earth and the Sun, making the side facing us dark. A student saying "it is behind the Earth" shows confusion about the orbital alignment required for the dark phase.

questions.q: If the Moon takes 29.5 days to complete its cycle, how long do you think it takes to go from a New Moon to a First Quarter phase?
questions.a: It takes approximately 7.4 days (one-fourth of the cycle). A student guessing "half a month" or "15 days" fails to connect the phases as segments of the total 29.5-day orbital period.

questions.q: Compare the Moon to a mirror. Is this a good comparison for why we see lunar phases?
questions.a: Yes, because the Moon reflects sunlight just as a mirror reflects light. A student who says "no" likely believes the Moon generates its own light, ignoring that stars are light sources but planets and moons are light reflectors.

questions.q: If you were on the Moon looking at the Earth, would the Earth have "phases" too?
questions.a: Yes, because the Earth would also be lit by the Sun at different angles from your perspective on the Moon. A student who says "no" is not applying the concept of light reflection and perspective to other objects in space.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment using a torch and a tennis ball to show a "waxing crescent" phase.
questions.a: The student should place the torch (Sun) to one side, move the ball (Moon) around their head (Earth), and position the ball so only a tiny sliver of the lit side is visible. A poor answer would just say "move the ball" without explaining how to align the light to create the specific crescent shape.
